title: Day & Night Around the World
strapline: When we're fast asleep, somewhere else the sun is just waking up.
intent: Exploring day and night gives children a first wonder-filled grasp that the world turns and the sun and moon come and go.
Comparing what people do by day and night, here and elsewhere, builds knowledge of routines, the world and time.
Light and dark play — torches, shadows, night skies — is rich, exciting sensory and scientific exploration.
Talking about their own bedtime and morning routines connects the theme to children's real lives.
The idea that it's night somewhere while it's day here opens awe at how big the world is.
implementation: Create a day-and-night contrast — a bright daytime area and a dark den with torches, stars and moon — to explore both.
Wonder together: 'When we're asleep, do you think everyone in the world is asleep too?'
Explore light and dark for real — shadows, torches, glow-in-the-dark, a starry ceiling — and talk about what we see.
Link it to children's routines — 'What do you do in the daytime? What happens at bedtime?' — and to animals of day and night.
Feed in knowledge lightly — the sun rises and sets, the moon and stars come out, the earth turns — kept simple and wondrous.
Follow the play — some children will chase shadows, others will play out day and night routines.
key_questions: What do you do in the daytime, and what happens at night?
When we're fast asleep, is it night everywhere in the world?
What can you see in the sky in the day, and at night?
Which animals come out at night?
How can we make a shadow — can you make yours grow?

impact.text: Children explore light and dark, shadows and torches, and talk about what they notice.
Children compare day and night and talk about their own routines.
Children begin to grasp that it can be day here and night elsewhere.
Children ask real questions about the sun, moon and stars.
Children play out day and night scenes with roles and shared ideas.

enhancements: A dark den with torches, glow stars, a moon and night-sky fabric.
A shadow-making station with a light source and objects to cast shadows.
Day-and-night sorting cards — sun, breakfast, playground / moon, stars, bedtime.
Nocturnal-animal small world alongside daytime animals.
A bedtime-routine role-play with pyjamas, teddies and storybooks.

playing_exploring: Children explore light, dark and shadows with fascination.
They play out day and night in their own way.
active_learning: Children experiment with torches and shadows to see what they can make happen.
They stay with the wonder of the night den and the sky.
creating_thinking: Children reason about day and night and where the sun goes.
They connect the theme to their own routines and the turning world.
